Why every man should learn
an instrument, even late
It trains your brain in a unique way. Reading notes, moving both hands and listening at the same time keeps your mind sharp.
It gives you something to look forward to. Practising a song after work is far more rewarding than another hour of screens.
It teaches patience. Progress is slow at first. Learning to enjoy small steps is a skill that helps everywhere in life.
It brings people together. Playing at a gathering or jamming with friends creates memories that last. Music connects.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Learning the story of music makes playing it more meaningful.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Learning the story of music makes playing it more meaningful.

slides.texte_overlay: Start with something simple. Guitar, piano or ukulele. A few lessons and ten minutes a day are enough to progress.
Don't wait to be good. Play songs you love from the start. Fun is what keeps you practising. Start with one song you love this week.
